base: Create a realistic production-quality UI design concept for the mobile loading screen of the existing anime Go game SigrikaGo. Target a 390 x 844 mobile viewport, single full-page portrait composition without device or browser chrome. Reference 1 is the approved original orange-haired character leaning on a desk: preserve her exact visual identity, face, costume, seated/leaning pose and the whole desk, do not redesign her or draw a chibi replacement. Reference 2 shows the current flawed loading composition only as content reference; improve hierarchy, do not clone the empty oversized cloud. References 3 and 4 are existing project home/story visual language: warm cream notebook paper #fffbf2, very faint paper grid, deep warm brown pen #4a3736, restrained blush pink #ff9ebb and pale cyan #9ad3de, hand-drawn stationery, no modern rounded card dashboard, no glass effects. Current date 2026-10-03; this UI has no dates. Keep the user's chosen elements: soft hand-drawn thought cloud above character slightly left; three small round connector bubbles routed outside character silhouette; upright-in-its-own-axis lightbulb tilted clockwise on the RIGHT side of her head, filled golden yellow from its base toward head at 65 percent; lightbulb is the sole progress meter, no extra progress bar; comic glow marks are hidden in this waiting state; original desk and Tip below it. Match cloud/bubbles/bulb outline ink hue and weight. Put a small believable Go life-and-death board illustration inside the thought cloud to judge occupied composition, grounded in the board shown in reference 4; this is illustrative mock content, no captions or answers. The only visible text is the exact existing tip below the desk: 'Tip：因为使用数子规则，建议下完单官再申请数目哦～' in two balanced readable lines, body 14-16 px UI font, hand-lettered Tip label. No title, buttons, navigation, badges, control panel, loading label, percentage, decorative confetti, stars or invented UI. Focus on intentional grouping, proportion and quiet negative space. Preserve full character image aspect ratio; do not stretch or crop the desk. This is a visual concept, not a runtime screenshot.

displayOrder.direction: Direction name: Compact thinking illustration. Use an open notebook-paper surface with a VERY faint grid, no card container. Make the approved character and desk about 94% of viewport width, sitting in the lower-middle part of screen, visually dominant and vivid. At upper left above her head, a compact cloud about 60-65% viewport width with a Go board inside; do not stretch it to almost full viewport width. Cluster cloud, round connecting bubbles and small bulb into a tight balanced triangular relationship around her head. Reduce the vacant distance between cloud and character, with bubbles wrapping her left silhouette. The character face should be the first thing noticed, then the Go board, then the bulb. Keep plenty of quiet cream space above the combined illustration, and a tidy two-line tip below the desk; warm and cozy like a club notebook illustration. Do not add paper borders, tape or extra doodles.

Direction name: Layered club notebook. Use a full-page cream notebook leaf, fine subtle paper grain and faint 20px grid as the sole background. Establish the cloud and Go diagram as a compact handwritten notebook annotation in the upper-middle, wider and slightly flatter than the compact illustration direction, around 75% viewport width with large rounded uneven lobes. Below, the original character and full desk fill 92% viewport width, with her head just under the thought annotation and the bulb close on the right. Three small round bubbles form a short curved connector in the left gap. Add a restrained warm-paper backing offset just 2-3px behind the cloud outline to echo the layered-paper motif seen in the project's dialogue, but no broad dark shadow. Treat the tip below desk as a narrow pale cream paper slip without a border or tape, integrated into the notebook. Very small blush/cyan stationery color accents in the paper layering only, no decorative icons. This direction should feel more like a tidy illustrated study page, with the Go study thought leading into the character, rather than a poster with unrelated floating icons. Preserve uncluttered base surface and exact character pose.

Direction name: Quiet manga thought panel. Use the same established cream-paper project style but a more asymmetric compact manga composition, all on the base surface without a surrounding panel border or app card. Put the original character and full desk in the lower middle, about 96% viewport width; arrange a softly irregular flattened cloud in the upper-left above her head, only about 62% viewport width, with a well-spaced small Go corner problem filling the cloud interior. Bias the cloud left and the small bulb right so they visually balance each other around the character. Make cloud, circle bubbles and bulb cleaner with the same dark-brown outline thickness, more confident pen lines with tiny hand-drawn irregularities, all interiors warm white. The lightbulb is only about 12% viewport width, about 65% yellow filled, sitting to the right of the character's temple in a comfortable clear gap. Three tiny circles wrap the hair on left. Warm cream background with almost invisible paper grain, no full-page grid in this direction except a faint partial grid texture receding around the composition. No notebook sheet edge, tape, arrows, extra stones outside the board, doodles, highlighter swashes, stickers, frame borders or shadows. Keep the entire thought/character/bulb scene vertically tight and centered in the middle 70% of viewport, intentional asymmetry rather than a stack of three rows. Tip remains below desk and uses clean readable UI body text with only the Tip label hand-lettered. The final image should feel calm, crisp and native to an anime Go game's hand-drawn loading interlude.

note: These are generated composition concepts; the runnable sample has not changed.
